parsed.study_design: Transdisciplinary mixed-methods case study combining hydrogeological analysis with socio-ethnological field observations and interviews
parsed.population_and_sample: Residents, water users, public authorities, regulators, and service providers in the Recife Metropolitan Region; the paper does not report a numerical interview or household sample size.
parsed.exposure: Fragmented multilevel water governance, deficient public supply and sanitation networks, rationing, groundwater regulation, and the public-private partnership for sewerage services.
parsed.outcome: Water-supply availability and continuity, unequal or poor connection, household coping strategies and alternative water sources, groundwater depletion, sanitation coverage, affordability risks, and water-related health hazards.
parsed.rationale: Sections 2.2–2.3 (pp. 5–7) empirically describe fragmented governance and heterogeneous household access strategies, including wells, storage, rainwater harvesting, and illegal network connections. Sections 3.1–3.3 (p. 8) report access-relevant outcomes such as rationing, supply-demand shortfalls, groundwater depletion, only 40% sewerage coverage, and sanitary risks; Section 4 (p. 9) identifies socio-ethnological investigation, field observations, and interviews as evidence sources.
